query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these travel-expense records.

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizes CIs into meaningful asset types (hardware, cloud, travel), giving a strong grouping axis. Values are well-grounded in the ci/short_description text (e.g. Dell Latitude -> hardware_endpoint, AWS EC2 -> cloud_service).

per_column.name: ci_form_factor
per_column.rationale: Finer-grained form factor (laptop/desktop/server) is derivable from ci strings and adds a useful sub-grouping. Partially redundant with asset_category but still a distinct axis. Well grounded.

per_column.name: travel_context
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant to the travel-expense query, separating travel vs non-travel items. Grounded in source text, though the dominance of 'not_travel' for hardware raises questions about whether these are truly travel expenses.

per_column.name: asset_brand
per_column.rationale: Brand extraction (Dell, HP, AWS, Samsonite) offers a genuine axis for spend/vendor analysis and is directly extractable from ci strings.

per_column.name: record_action_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes lifecycle action (procurement/registration/provisioning) from short_description; a reasonable inference and useful for grouping. Some categories (allocation, maintenance_upgrade) rely on inference but appear warranted.

per_column.name: creation_method
per_column.rationale: Manual vs automated is clearly cued by phrases like 'Automated creation'/'Automatically generated'. A binary flag but offers a legitimate comparison axis; well grounded.

per_column.name: processing_lag_band
per_column.rationale: Bands the lag between opened_at and processed_date, a useful operational-efficiency axis. Derivable from date columns; 'not_processed' correctly handles nan dates.

per_column.name: source_id_present
per_column.rationale: A bare presence/absence flag on an existing column; low analytical leverage and largely trivial, though correctly grounded.

per_column.name: department_group
per_column.rationale: Appears near-redundant with the existing 'department' column. More concerning, department is not present in the sampled source_text yet specific groups (Customer_Support, Sales) are asserted per row, so groundedness cannot be confirmed and values may be invented relative to shown evidence.

per_column.name: is_miscellaneous_ci
per_column.rationale: Near-constant flag (483 false / 17 true) with little discriminating power for this query. Grounded but low leverage.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine new axes (asset_category, form_factor, brand, travel_context, action_type, processing_lag) that are well-grounded in the ci and short_description text, directly supporting analysis of these expense records. A few columns are weak: source_id_present and is_miscellaneous_ci add little leverage, and department_group is largely redundant with an existing column while asserting per-row department values not visible in the sampled source text, raising a groundedness concern. Overall the set is useful and mostly grounded.
